literal: Zhang Zuan; Zhang Liang; Zhang Yao; Zhao Qi; Xu Yuan; Wang Jun; Wang Hong
idiomatic: Zhang Zuan; Zhang Liang; Zhang Yao; Zhao Qi; Xu Yuan; Wang Jun; Wang Hong

literal: Zhang Zuan, styled Huizuan, was a native of Pingcheng in Dai Commandery.
idiomatic: Zhang Zuan, styled Huizuan, came from Pingcheng in Dai Commandery.

literal: His father Lie was governor of Sanggan.
idiomatic: His father Lie had been governor of Sanggan.

literal: Zuan first served Erzhu Rong, then became chief of staff to Erzhu Zhao's headquarters.
idiomatic: Zuan first served Erzhu Rong, then became chief of staff on Erzhu Zhao's staff.

literal: Zhao sent him to the Grand Ancestor, and he came to be noticed and favored.
idiomatic: Zhao sent him to Gao Huan, and he won notice and favor.

literal: When the Grand Ancestor raised the righteous standard in Shandong, Liu Dan held Xiang Province in resistance; Zuan was then among them.
idiomatic: When Gao Huan raised the standard in Shandong, Liu Dan held Xiang Province and resisted; Zuan was among the defenders.

literal: The Grand Ancestor attacked and took it, and made Zuan a staff officer on the chancellor's military staff.
idiomatic: Gao Huan attacked and took the city, then made Zuan a staff officer on the chancellor's army.

literal: Zuan was obliging and unorthodox by nature; coming and going at his side, he gradually won intimate treatment, and was then appointed mobile headquarters gentleman.
idiomatic: Zuan was accommodating by nature and quick at his errands. Moving in and out at Gao Huan's side, he gradually won intimate favor and was appointed gentleman of the mobile headquarters.

literal: The Grand Ancestor memorialized to reduce state enfeoffments and distribute rewards to civil and military officials; Zuan was enfeoffed Marquis of Shouzhang according to precedent.
idiomatic: Gao Huan memorialized to trim state enfeoffments and reward civil and military officials; Zuan received the usual grant and was enfeoffed marquis of Shouzhang.

literal: Late in Emperor Wu of Wei's reign, the Grand Ancestor went to Luoyang; he made the Duke of Zhao Commandery Chen mobile headquarters to guard Jinyang, and made Zuan right vice director.
idiomatic: Late in the reign of Emperor Wu of Wei, Gao Huan went to Luoyang. He left the Duke of Zhao Commandery Chen as mobile headquarters at Jinyang and made Zuan his right vice director.

literal: He was transferred to merit staff officer of the chancellor's office and appointed right grand master for splendid happiness.
idiomatic: He was transferred to merit staff officer in the chancellor's office and appointed right grand master for splendid happiness.

literal: Sent on mission to the Rouran; for carrying out orders he won praise.
idiomatic: Sent on mission to the Rouran, he carried out his commission to satisfaction and won praise.

literal: He served successively as gentleman attendant at the central and outer offices and at the chancellor's office.
idiomatic: He served in turn as gentleman attendant at the central and outer offices and at the chancellor's office.

literal: At the battle of Mount Mang there was a great capture of prisoners; the Grand Ancestor ordered Zuan to escort them to the capital; the Wei emperor bestowed five hundred bolts of silk and enfeoffed him Baron of Wu'an County.
idiomatic: At Mount Mang the army took many prisoners. Gao Huan ordered Zuan to escort them to the capital. The Wei emperor bestowed five hundred bolts of silk and enfeoffed him baron of Wu'an County.

literal: Again he became right vice director of the Grand Ancestor's mobile headquarters and followed the campaign against Yubi.
idiomatic: He again became right vice director on Gao Huan's mobile headquarters and followed the campaign against Yubi.

literal: As the great army was about to return to Shandong, reaching Jin Province, it suddenly met cold rain; the soldiers were hungry and freezing, and some died.
idiomatic: As the great army was returning to Shandong it reached Jin Province and was struck by cold rain. The troops went hungry and cold; some died.

literal: The province, because of frontier prohibitions, would not allow entry into the city.
idiomatic: Because of frontier restrictions the province would not let them enter the city.

literal: At that time Zuan was on separate mission; when he encountered them he at once ordered the gates opened to admit them, billeted them among the people, and supplied fire and food — many were saved.
idiomatic: Zuan was then on separate mission. When he came upon them he ordered the gates opened at once, lodged the men in private homes, and gave them fire and food. Many were saved.

literal: The Grand Ancestor heard and approved.
idiomatic: Gao Huan heard of it and approved.

literal: Zuan served the Grand Ancestor more than twenty years, transmitting orders and instructions, and was greatly favored.
idiomatic: Zuan served Gao Huan for more than twenty years, passing on his orders and instructions, and was held in great favor.

literal: When the Heir Apparent succeeded, Hou Jing rebelled in Yingchuan and drew in Western Wei.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng succeeded, Hou Jing rebelled in Yingchuan and called in Western Wei.

literal: Zuan was made south-route mobile headquarters and with the generals led the punitive campaign.
idiomatic: Zuan was made south-route mobile headquarters and marched with the generals to suppress him.

literal: On his return he was appointed inspector of Ying Province.
idiomatic: On his return he was appointed inspector of Ying Province.

literal: It happened that the Heir Apparent entered [the capital] as junior tutor of the heir apparent.
idiomatic: It happened that Gao Cheng entered [the capital] as junior tutor of the heir apparent.

literal: Later, with the Prince of Pingyuan Duan Xiaoxian, mobile headquarters inspector of the masters of writing Xin Shu, and others, he besieged Eastern Chu; he then took Guangling, Jing Province, and several cities and beheaded the bandit chieftain Dongfang Baie.
idiomatic: Later, with Prince of Pingyuan Duan Xiaoxian, mobile headquarters inspector of the masters of writing Xin Shu, and others, he besieged Eastern Chu, then took Guangling, Jing Province, and several cities and beheaded the bandit chieftain Dongfang Baie.

literal: He was granted equal in protocol to three imperators, made commissioner for building the Great Wall, and commanded several thousand foot and horse to guard the northern border.
idiomatic: He was granted equal in protocol to three imperators, made commissioner for building the Great Wall, and commanded several thousand foot and horse to guard the northern frontier.

literal: On his return he was promoted to guards general; soon he died.
idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to guards general; soon afterward he died.

literal: Zhang Liang, styled Bode, was a native of Yincheng in Xihe.
idiomatic: Zhang Liang, styled Bode, came from Yincheng in Xihe.

literal: In youth he had ability and usefulness.
idiomatic: From youth he showed ability and resolve.

literal: He first served Erzhu Zhao and was appointed general who pacifies the distant.
idiomatic: He first served Erzhu Zhao and was appointed general who pacifies the distant.

literal: For merit he was enfeoffed Baron of Yincheng with a fief of five hundred households.
idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed baron of Yincheng with a fief of five hundred households.

literal: The Grand Ancestor attacked Zhao at Jinyang; Zhao fled to Xiurong.
idiomatic: Gao Huan attacked Zhao at Jinyang; Zhao fled to Xiurong.

literal: Zhao's close associates all secretly sent pledges of loyalty; only Liang sent no memorial.
idiomatic: Zhao's close associates all secretly sent pledges of loyalty; only Liang sent no letter.

literal: When Zhao was defeated he hid in remote mountains and ordered Liang and the steward Chen Shanti to cut off his head to surrender; none could bear to do it, and Zhao then hanged himself on a tree.
idiomatic: When Zhao was defeated he hid in the mountains and ordered Liang and his steward Chen Shanti to cut off his head and surrender. Neither could bear to do it. Zhao then hanged himself from a tree.

literal: Bode knelt by the corpse and wept.
idiomatic: Bode knelt by the corpse and wept.

literal: The Grand Ancestor praised and sighed at this.
idiomatic: Gao Huan praised him and sighed with admiration.

literal: He was appointed staff officer of the chancellor's office, gradually received intimate treatment, and was entrusted with secretary duties.
idiomatic: He was appointed staff officer in the chancellor's office, gradually won intimate favor, and was put in charge of correspondence.

literal: During Tianping he was the Heir Apparent's mobile headquarters gentleman, in charge of the seven military bureaus.
idiomatic: During Tianping he was Gao Cheng's mobile headquarters gentleman, in charge of the seven military bureaus.

literal: Though a headquarters gentleman, he was constantly at the Grand Ancestor's side.
idiomatic: Though a headquarters gentleman, he was constantly at Gao Huan's side.

literal: He was promoted to right vice director of the mobile headquarters.
idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice director of the mobile headquarters.

literal: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled, he and Grand Marshal Hulu Jin guarded Heyang.
idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled, he and Grand Marshal Hulu Jin guarded Heyang.

literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou at the upper stream set fire ships to burn the river bridge.
idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou upstream sent fire ships to burn the river bridge.

literal: Liang then prepared over a hundred small boats, all carrying long chains with nails on the chain heads.
idiomatic: Liang then prepared more than a hundred small boats, each carrying long chains tipped with nails.

literal: When the fire ships approached he at once sent out the small boats, nailed them fast, and drew the chains toward shore so the fire ships could not reach the bridge.
idiomatic: When the fire ships drew near he sent out the small boats at once, nailed them in place, and hauled the chains to shore so the fire ships could not reach the bridge.

literal: That the bridge was preserved was Liang's plan.
idiomatic: The bridge was saved by Liang's plan.

literal: Early in Wuding he was appointed grand master for splendid happiness in the central government.
idiomatic: Early in Wuding he was appointed grand master for splendid happiness.

literal: Xue Jun once dreamed of Liang on a mountain holding silk; he told Liang and divined, saying: "Silk on a mountain — the character for 'hidden' (you).
idiomatic: Xue Jun once dreamed of Liang on a mountain holding silk. He told Liang and divined, saying, "Silk on a mountain — that is the character for 'hidden' (you).

literal: Will you become inspector of You Province?
idiomatic: Will you become inspector of You Province?

literal: " Several months later Liang went out as inspector of You Province.
idiomatic: " Several months later Liang was sent out as inspector of You Province.

literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, he was made general who pacifies the south and governor of Liang Province.
idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, he was appointed general who pacifies the south and governor of Liang Province.

literal: Soon he was additionally made commander of military affairs for eleven provinces including Yang and Ying, concurrently mobile headquarters director of palace masters in the interior, then transferred to commander of military affairs for eight provinces including the two Yu, Yang, and Ying, grand general who campaigns west, inspector of Yu, right vice director of the masters of writing, and southwest-route mobile headquarters.
idiomatic: Soon he was additionally commander of military affairs for eleven provinces including Yang and Ying, concurrently mobile headquarters director of palace masters in the interior, then transferred to commander of eight provinces including the two Yu, Yang, and Ying, grand general who campaigns west, inspector of Yu, right vice director of the masters of writing, and southwest-route mobile headquarters.

literal: He attacked Liang's Jiangxia, Yingyang, and seven other cities; all were taken.
idiomatic: He attacked Liang's Jiangxia, Yingyang, and seven other cities; all fell.

literal: Liang was upright and plain by nature, diligent and forceful, and was deeply trusted by the Grand Ancestor and the Heir Apparent, who entrusted him with innermost duties.
idiomatic: Liang was plain and upright by nature, diligent and forceful. Gao Huan and Gao Cheng trusted him deeply and gave him duties at the heart of power.

literal: Yet he lacked refinement, loved wealth, and though long at their side could not remain incorrupt; in every province he held office there were reports of bribery.
idiomatic: Yet he lacked refinement and loved profit. Long at their side he could not stay clean, and in every province he held there were reports of corrupt taking.

literal: At the end of Wuding he was summoned as palace attendant and chief rectifier of Fen Province.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he was summoned as palace attendant and chief rectifier of Fen Province.

literal: Early in Tianbao he was appointed grand warden of glory, added grand general of the flying cavalry and equal in protocol to three imperators, separately enfeoffed baron of Anding, and transferred to commander of the palace guards.
idiomatic: Early in Tianbao he was appointed grand warden of glory, given the added titles grand general of the flying cavalry and equal in protocol to three imperators, separately enfeoffed baron of Anding, and transferred to commander of the palace guards.

literal: Soon he died in office and was posthumously granted Duke of Works.
idiomatic: Soon he died in office and was posthumously granted duke of works.

literal: Zhang Yao, styled Lingguang, was a native of Changping in Shanggu.
idiomatic: Zhang Yao, styled Lingguang, came from Changping in Shanggu.

literal: His father Feng was chief clerk of Jin Province.
idiomatic: His father Feng had been chief clerk of Jin Province.

literal: Yao from youth was upright and careful and well understood historical and administrative duties.
idiomatic: From youth Yao was upright and careful and knew the work of records and administration well.

literal: On first appointment he was attendant within the palace gates; he was transferred to water bureau attendant staff officer of the Ministry of Education.
idiomatic: On first appointment he was attendant within the palace gates, then transferred to water bureau attendant staff officer under the Ministry of Education.

literal: When the righteous standard was raised the Grand Ancestor promoted him to chief clerk of General-in-Chief Han Gui's headquarters.
idiomatic: When the righteous standard was raised Gao Huan promoted him to chief clerk on General-in-Chief Han Gui's staff.

literal: When Gui was made inspector of Ying and Ji, Yao was again made Gui's consulting staff officer.
idiomatic: When Gui was made inspector of Ying and Ji, Yao again served as his consulting staff officer.

literal: Later he was impeached by the censor; prefectural staff and Gui's close associates — over a hundred caught in the net on corruption charges — only Yao was clear and alone escaped.
idiomatic: Later the censors impeached the case. More than a hundred prefectural staff and men close to Gui were caught in the net on corruption charges; only Yao was clear and escaped alone.

literal: He was summoned as warehouse clerk of the chancellor's office.
idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as warehouse clerk in the chancellor's office.

literal: When the Manifest Ancestor succeeded to affairs he was moved to headquarters staff.
idiomatic: When Gao Yang succeeded to power he was moved to headquarters staff.

literal: Early in Tianbao he was granted baron of Duting Township and acted in charge of the warehouse and treasury bureaus.
idiomatic: Early in Tianbao he was granted baron of Duting township and put in acting charge of the warehouse and treasury bureaus.

literal: Whenever there were bestowals Yao was usually put in charge.
idiomatic: Whenever there were grants and gifts Yao was usually put in charge.

literal: He was transferred to secretary of the palace library and promoted to right vice director of the masters of writing.
idiomatic: He was transferred to secretary of the palace library and promoted to right vice director of the masters of writing.

literal: The Manifest Ancestor once went out on a nearby trip and had Yao remain on guard.
idiomatic: Gao Yang once went out on a short trip and left Yao to hold the palace.

literal: The emperor returned at night; Yao did not open the gates in time and drilled the troops in strict readiness.
idiomatic: The emperor returned at night. Yao did not open the gates at once but drilled the troops and stood ready.

literal: The emperor halted outside the gate a long time and pressed urgently.
idiomatic: The emperor halted outside the gate a long while and pressed him urgently.

literal: Yao said that because the night was deep true and false were hard to distinguish, he had to see the face by fire before the gates could open; he therefore went out alone to see the emperor.
idiomatic: Yao said that in the deep of night true and false were hard to tell; he had to see the emperor's face by torchlight before the gates could open. He therefore went out alone to meet him.

literal: The emperor laughed and said: "Do you wish to imitate Zhi Junzhang?
idiomatic: The emperor laughed and said, "Do you mean to imitate Zhi Junzhang?

literal: " He then had Yao go forward to open the gates and then entered; he deeply praised and rewarded him and bestowed brocade silks.
idiomatic: " He then had Yao go forward and open the gates before he entered, praised him deeply, and bestowed brocade silks.

literal: He was sent out as inspector of South Qing Province but did not take up the post.
idiomatic: He was sent out as inspector of South Qing Province but never took up the post.

literal: When Emperor Suizong assisted the government Yao was repeatedly promoted to director of the palace library.
idiomatic: When Emperor Suizong assisted the government Yao rose repeatedly to director of the palace library.

literal: Zhao Qi, styled Xingluo, was a native of Guangping.
idiomatic: Zhao Qi, styled Xingluo, came from Guangping.

literal: His father Da was recording clerk of You Province.
idiomatic: His father Da had been recording clerk of You Province.

literal: Qi was deep, careful, and capable.
idiomatic: Qi was deep, careful, and capable.

literal: When the righteous standard was raised the Grand Ancestor made Duan Rong inspector of Ding and made Qi Rong's secretariat chief; he was appointed cavalier attendant for the carriage.
idiomatic: When the righteous standard was raised Gao Huan made Duan Rong inspector of Ding and made Qi Rong's secretariat chief; Qi was appointed cavalier attendant for the carriage.

literal: During Tianping he was summoned as horse bureau clerk of the chancellor's office and was repeatedly promoted to palace gentleman for scattering ailments.
idiomatic: During Tianping he was summoned to the horse bureau of the chancellor's office and rose repeatedly to palace gentleman for scattering ailments.

literal: When the Heir Apparent succeeded to affairs Qi was sent out as inspector of Jian and was repeatedly promoted to palace attendant.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng succeeded Qi was sent out as inspector of Jian and rose repeatedly to palace attendant.

literal: Qi, across the Grand Ancestor's generation, repeatedly held the two cavalry bureaus of the chancellor's office and was in charge of horses and troops for more than ten years.
idiomatic: Across Gao Huan's generation Qi repeatedly held the two cavalry bureaus of the chancellor's office and managed horses and troops for more than ten years.

literal: After the Manifest Ancestor assumed the throne Qi left provincial office and returned to court; though he held ranks of the nine ministers and palace attendant, he always kept his original post supervising troops, coming and going at command, trusted as an inner confidant, second only to the two Zhangs.
idiomatic: After Gao Yang took the throne Qi left the provinces and returned to court. Though he held ranks of the nine ministers and palace attendant, he always kept his original post supervising troops, going in and out at command, trusted at the heart of power — second only to the two Zhangs.

literal: He was sent out as inspector of West Yan Province, investigated and prohibited [wrongdoing], and after more than a year was dismissed when nothing was proved.
idiomatic: He was sent out as inspector of West Yan Province, where he investigated and enforced prohibitions. After more than a year he was dismissed when the charges could not be proved.

literal: In the second year of Heqing he was summoned back to Jinyang.
idiomatic: In the second year of Heqing he was summoned back to Jinyang.

literal: In the third year he was additionally made minister of sacrificial worships and opener of government.
idiomatic: In the third year he was additionally made minister of sacrificial worships and opener of government.

literal: Early in Tiantong he was transferred to chamberlain for imperial ceremonial with a salary allotment from Langye Commandery.
idiomatic: Early in Tiantong he was transferred to chamberlain for imperial ceremonial and drew his salary allotment from Langye Commandery.

literal: In the second year he was made inspector of Cang and added commander of six provinces.
idiomatic: In the second year he was made inspector of Cang and added commander of six provinces.

literal: Midway through Wuping he died in office.
idiomatic: Midway through Wuping he died in office.

literal: Xu Yuan, styled Yanxia, was a native of Shimen in Guangning.
idiomatic: Xu Yuan, styled Yanxia, came from Shimen in Guangning.

literal: His ancestors originally came from Guangping.
idiomatic: His ancestors had originally come from Guangping.

literal: His great-grandfather Ding was general of the army in Yun and garrison chief of Pingshuo; the family then settled at Shuo.
idiomatic: His great-grandfather Ding had been general of the army in Yun and garrison chief of Pingshuo; the family then settled at Shuo.

literal: Yuan in youth studied clerical affairs; the commandery recruited him as merit officer.
idiomatic: In youth Yuan studied clerical work; the commandery recruited him as merit officer.

literal: Before long, with the inspector he led households to the righteous standard; he was appointed defense commander of the city and made magistrate of Yingtao.
idiomatic: Before long he went with the inspector, leading local households to the righteous standard. He was appointed defense commander of the city and made magistrate of Yingtao.

literal: The Grand Ancestor, because Yuan was skilled in documents and accounts, appointed him cavalry staff officer of the chancellor's office; he was often on campaigns, succeeded in military affairs, and was deeply known to the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: Because Yuan was skilled in documents and accounts Gao Huan appointed him cavalry staff officer in the chancellor's office. He was often on campaign, handled military affairs well, and came to be well known to Gao Huan.

literal: He successively served as inspector of Julu and Chenliu.
idiomatic: He served in turn as inspector of Julu and Chenliu.

literal: Early in Tianbao he was impeached by the censor; he met an amnesty and was pardoned and was suspended for two years.
idiomatic: Early in Tianbao the censors impeached him. He met an amnesty and was pardoned, then lay idle for two years.

literal: The Manifest Ancestor, because Yuan was a meritorious veteran, specially made him chief clerk of the palace guards headquarters; he was repeatedly promoted to inspector of East Xu and entered [the capital] as grand master for splendid happiness.
idiomatic: Because Yuan was a meritorious veteran Gao Yang specially made him chief clerk of the palace guards headquarters. He rose repeatedly to inspector of East Xu and entered [the capital] as grand master for splendid happiness.
